t: Lattice's own board for its biggest ECP5 FPGA chip.
steps: Buy the board from Mouser or another electronics distributor. The kit includes a mini USB cable and a 12 volt adapter.
Install the open tools Yosys, nextpnr, and Project Trellis, or use Lattice Diamond with the bundled one-year license.
Short jumper JP2 to send the 12 MHz clock to the FPGA.
Plug in the 12 volt adapter and the USB cable.
Build the ecp5_evn example from Project Trellis.
Load the design and watch the LEDs sweep.
Next, try the soc_ecp5_evn RISC-V example.
Stick to tested designs at first. The Trellis docs warn that experimental bitstreams could harm a board.
meta: Open Board. From $99.50. A few stores.
